problems.recorded: No estimate. The joint human-AI idea-quantity comparison is excluded in not_extracted under S1-O5 because its idea set and supporting numerical statistics are not specified.
problems.printed: The discussion reports that humans working jointly with AI produced significantly more ideas than humans working alone. No numerical test, effect size, or arm means are supplied there for this joint-output contrast.
problems.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 427), section 5.1, final paragraph beginning "For our setting".
problems.quote: For our setting, we find that the human working with the AI jointly produced significantly more ideas as compared to alone.
problems.note: Extraction rule 4 requires every eligible full-sample outcome contrast; codebook section 8 explicitly accommodates contrasts described only in words. This is a reported fluency comparison between the randomized human+AI and human-only conditions, distinct from the extracted human-authored idea-count comparison. Add a with_ai / fluency / ai_vs_bau estimate for joint idea quantity, retain the narrative result, and leave unavailable numerical statistics null. Preserve the uncertainty about whether this claim concerns accepted ideas or all logged ideas in the notes. That uncertainty prevents assigning the logged totals in Table 2 to this contrast; it does not justify omitting the reported comparison. Do not derive arm means, a p-value, or a test statistic from the narrative or the logged totals.

summary: Checked all four recorded estimates against their cited PDF pages and read all 380 lines of the markdown conversion, including the references; the ten-page paper contains no appendix. Confirmed the analyzed counts (26 per arm, 52 total), the three Mann-Whitney results, the rank-biserial correlation, and the human-authored idea means, with the correct outcomes and arms. The recorded question, construct, measure, unit, direction, AI availability, timing, within-person status, comparison type, and uncertainty basis are supported. No numerical transcription errors were found. One eligible narrative contrast is missing: joint human-AI idea quantity versus human-only. Unaccepted AI suggestion totals, pooled AI-versus-human origin comparisons, process analyses, self-reports, and the correlation between output measures do not supply additional eligible estimates. The paper reports no eligible across_people or after_ai contrast.
